title: Unsupervised deep learning screen finds D3 agonists boost zebrafish sociality
summary: ZeChat, an assay based on unsupervised deep learning that classifies zebrafish social behavior, was used to screen a neuroactive compound library. Different chemical classes produced distinct behavioral fingerprints, and dopamine D3 agonists (pramipexole, piribedil, 7-hydroxy-DPAT-HBr) stimulated sociality and rescued social deficits in a valproic acid-induced zebrafish autism model. Evidence is limited to zebrafish and the abstract gives no sample sizes. Preprint of 2021-09-25.
ai_technology: Unsupervised deep learning classification of high-dimensional zebrafish social behavior (ZeChat)

evidence.tested: Compound library screen followed by in vivo testing of three D3 agonists, including rescue in a valproic acid zebrafish model.
evidence.unknown: Relevance to human sociality or autism is not established; sample sizes not stated in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised deep learning classified social behavior phenotypes, enabling the screen that nominated D3 agonists.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations were not available. Publisher full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
